attributes.body_ja:
「では」と「じゃあ」は、どちらも「それでは」を短（みじか）くした接続詞（せつぞくし）です。この表現（ひょうげん）は「それ」と格助詞（かくじょし）「で」、そして副助詞（ふくじょし）の「は」の組（く）み合（あ）わせとも考（かんが）えられますが、ふつうは一（ひと）つの単語（たんご）のように扱（あつか）われます。「それでは」「では」「じゃあ」の順番（じゅんばん）で、かたい言（い）い方（かた）からくだけた言（い）い方（かた）になります。

「それでは」には、主（おも）に二（ふた）つの使（つか）い方（かた）があります。一（ひと）つは、相手（あいて）の話（はなし）を聞（き）いてから、自分（じぶん）が考（かんが）えたことを伝（つた）える使（つか）い方（かた）です。もう一（ひと）つは、「話題（わだい）を (A) から (B) に移（うつ）す、いいタイミングだ」のようなニュアンスで、話題（わだい）を変（か）える使（つか）い方（かた）です。

一（ひと）つ目（め）の使（つか）い方（かた）は、相手（あいて）の話（はなし）を受（う）けて、自分（じぶん）が出（だ）した結論（けつろん）や、「こうかな？」と思（おも）うことを伝（つた）えるときによく使（つか）われます。

豆知識（まめちしき）

「それでは」「では」「じゃあ」には、場面（ばめん）を変（か）える働（はたら）きがあるので、別（わか）れの挨拶（あいさつ）をするときにもよく使（つか）われます。
attributes.body:
では and じゃあ are both abbreviations of それでは, and used as conjunctions in Japanese. This structure may be considered as a combination of それ, the case marking particle で, and the binding (adverbial) particle は, but is commonly treated as a single word. それでは, では and じゃ is the order of use from most formal to least formal.

それでは has two primary functions. It can be used to continue in the same topic, showing that '(B) is a result of (A)'. Or it may be used to change the conversation topic completely, showing that '(A) is at a good point to become (B)'. In each of these cases, it can be translated as 'and with that' in English. 'If so', 'well then', and 'in that case' are also common translations.

The translation of 'in that case' is most commonly used when one person is making an assumption/drawing a conclusion about something that someone else has just said.

Fun Fact

それでは, では, and じゃあ are also frequently used as a polite way to say 'goodbye'. In these situations, it comes across in a similar way to 'well…. I best be off' in English.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

attributes.body: それなら and それでは can both be used at the start of a sentence as transition markers meaning in that case or well then. それなら expresses a response to a specific condition, as in それなら行きません (In that case, I won’t go). それでは can overlap in usage, but it can also mean well then or and with that, often used to wrap up a topic, as in それでは、失礼します (Well then, excuse me), which それなら cannot convey.3

attributes.body: Both can appear at the beginning of a sentence to mark a transition. では・それでは・じゃあ signal a shift or next step based on context, e.g. じゃあ、行こうか ('Well then, shall we go?') さ (often extended as さあ) adds an encouraging or prompting tone, e.g. さあ、そろそろ行こうか！ ('Come on, let's get going!')

attributes.body: Both mark transitions, but with slightly different nuance. さて is used to shift to a new topic or proceed to the next step, e.g. さて、次の話題に入りましょう ('Now then, let's move on to the next topic.') では・それでは・じゃあ reference the previous context and often lead into a decision or conclusion, similar to 'well then' or 'in that case', e.g. それでは、始めましょう ('Well then, let's begin.')
